lines.text: PATCH is the inside of the sound.
One patch, in full, and playable while you take it apart.
This is a whole patch: real modules, joined by cables.
Sound flows left to right along the green ones.
A stack of saws makes the tone, a filter softens it, and a chorus widens it.
The last plate is always the envelope and the output.
Amber cables carry movement. This one is a slow LFO, sweeping the filter.
Every knob sits where it really is, in hertz, milliseconds and decibels.
The play button plays the standard sample: five seconds, the same for every patch.
That makes patches fair to compare. To judge a sound, play it.
Above the rack, the model guesses how likely you are to prefer this patch, and says why.
Point at a module, and the strip below says what it does, and what the model can't hear.
A chorus's width, for one, is invisible to it.
Turn any knob while you play, and the sound follows your hand.
Bypass a module, and it steps out of the sound.
Pull a cable, and the socket goes quiet. What it carried waits in HELD.
Command-Z puts it back.
The node bank holds forty-two modules, in the order sound flows through them.
Click one, and it's in your hand. Every socket it fits lights up, and says what it would do.
Rest on a socket and press play, to hear it before anything changes.
Click the socket, and it's in.
A new sound source lights amber instead, because it would replace what's there.
Movement can come from a chain.
A sample and hold picks random values, a quantizer snaps them to A minor, and a slew glides between them.
Hold one key, and you get a melody.
Drop a shaper on a busy slot, and it wraps what's there instead of replacing it.
Steps is a sequencer for timbre.
Put it on a filter and draw up to eight bars. The tone plays them as a pattern.
Sync locks the pattern to the tempo, here 84.
Love part of a sound? Lock it: a knob by its dot, or a whole module by its square.
Then press Evolve from this.
Only what you left unlocked can change, and the new patch lands on the bench.
Your edits wait until you commit.
Commit plays the original and your edit, in random order, and asks which is better.
Either answer teaches the model.
Already sure? Tick my edit is better, and it's filed as a claim.
Export a patch as a file, or as a picture of the rack.
The picture carries the patch inside. Drop either onto Auracle, and it opens, ready to play.
And EVOLVE's lineage keeps the history: each edit, each evolution, and what changed.
All of it at once, at 84.
Shape the filter as it plays.
Add some grit after it.
Lock the filter, and commit it as yours.
Read it, change it, grow it, protect it, and keep what's yours.
Next, EVOLVE: breeding sounds you like.
